docRequirement: memory.md:161 binds the instruction-injection seam: "Block-level HTML comments (`<!-- maintainer notes -->`) in CLAUDE.md files are stripped before the content is injected into Claude's context." The same line carries two qualifiers that constrain the fix: "Comments inside code blocks are preserved" and "When you open a CLAUDE.md file directly with the Read tool, comments remain visible" — so the strip happens at injection, not at file read. memory.md:388 extends the identical rule to the auto-memory index: "YAML frontmatter and block-level HTML comments are stripped before the index is loaded, so they don't count toward the limits" (the 200-line / 25KB MEMORY.md load limits of memory.md:383).
current: No HTML-comment stripping exists on any injection seam. (1) Pinned block: `composePinnedCapabilityContext` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:960) reads each instruction layer with `runtime.materializer.readText(layer.resource)` (base-agent.ts:967) and pushes it unmodified — `bodies.push(`<capability-layer key=...>\n${content}\n</capability-layer>`)` at base-agent.ts:974. Memory/rule layers (base-agent.ts:977-1014) remove exactly two things: `@import` lines via `parseMemoryImportPath` (base-agent.ts:1003-1007) and rule frontmatter via `unscopedRuleBody` (base-agent.ts:997, memory-store.ts:270-274, parser at memory-store.ts:214). (2) The reader underneath is byte-verbatim: `readText` in packages/shared/src/capabilities/materializer.ts:169-186 returns `readFileSync(contentPath)` decoded as utf-8 after a revision/hash staleness check, nothing else. (3) Lazy nested instruction files: `readNestedInstructionBody` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:865-878) only trims and truncates at `MAX_NESTED_INSTRUCTION_FILE_BYTES` (native-sources.ts:772), and the body is injected verbatim as `<instructions file=...>` at base-agent.ts:1258-1262. (4) Auto-memory load limit: `readMemoryFile` (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:29-32) slices the first `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200` (memory-store.ts:8) RAW lines — frontmatter and comment lines included in the count — and there is no 25KB cap anywhere (`grep -ran 'MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT|25 \* 1024|MEMORY_LOAD_BYTE'` over packages/apps returns only memory-store.ts:8/29/68). (5) The only `<!-- -->` handling in shared source is `AUTO_MEMORY_MARKER_REGEX_SOURCE = '<!-- nessy:auto:(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}) -->'` and `stripAutoMemoryMarkers` (memory-store.ts:159-163), which removes that one marker; the other repo hits are packages/shared/src/docs/source-guides.ts:79/98 (`<!-- SETUP: -->` / `<!-- KNOWLEDGE: -->` guide splitting) and packages/session-tools-core/src/templates/loader.ts:61 (leading comment parsed as template metadata) — neither is a general stripper. The files affected really are ours to strip: packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:82 `PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES = ['AGENTS.md', 'CLAUDE.md', 'CLAUDE.local.md']`. The Claude SDK backend is not a rescue — packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:305 keeps `settingSources: ['user', 'project', 'local']` so upstream loads its own (stripped) copy, while our pinned copy of the same files still carries the comments.
divergence: The mechanism is absent, not misnamed and not narrower: zero of the three injection seams (pinned instruction layers, pinned memory/rule layers, lazily delivered nested instruction files) removes an HTML comment, so `<!-- maintainer notes -->` reach the model verbatim on every capability generation. Second half of the same rule: comment and frontmatter lines are counted by the 200-line MEMORY.md slice instead of being stripped before measurement (memory-store.ts:29-32), which is the exact behaviour memory.md:388 describes as the pre-v2.1.211 bug. Note what is NOT wrong: frontmatter IS already stripped from rule files at injection (unscopedRuleBody), and the `@import` filter proves the seam for line-level filtering already exists — the fix slots in beside it.

change.what: Add `export function stripBlockHtmlComments(text: string): string` — a fence-aware, BLOCK-LEVEL-ONLY stripper. Walk lines tracking fenced code blocks (``` and ~~~, opening fence length must be matched or exceeded to close, info string ignored) and never strip inside a fence, per 'Comments inside code blocks are preserved'. Outside fences, remove a comment only when `<!--` is the first non-whitespace on its line; consume through the line whose last non-whitespace is `-->` (multi-line comments included); drop the consumed lines entirely rather than leaving blanks, and collapse the resulting 3+ blank-line runs to one. Leave a mid-line/trailing `<!-- ... -->` alone — it is not block-level, and our own inline `<!-- nessy:auto:YYYY-MM-DD -->` marker (memory-store.ts:159) MUST survive this helper so `stripAutoMemoryMarkers` and memory-cleanup keep working. Then change `readMemoryFile` (line 29-32) to strip YAML frontmatter and block comments BEFORE the 200-line slice (memory.md:388), i.e. read the file, drop a leading `---`-delimited block, `stripBlockHtmlComments`, then `.split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)`. Do NOT add the 25KB cap here — see notes.

Two call sites, both one line each. At line 967-974 wrap the instruction-layer body: `const content = stripBlockHtmlComments(await runtime.materializer.readText(layer.resource))` before it is pushed as `<capability-layer>`; keep the `eagerInstructionFiles` push unconditional so InstructionsLoaded still reports a file that became empty. At line 997-1014 apply the same helper to `body` before the existing `@import` filter, so `withoutImports` is computed on stripped text (this also means an `@import` written inside a comment stops being followed, which matches Claude stripping first). Import the helper from './memory/memory-store.ts' alongside the existing `parseMemoryImportPath, parseRuleFile, unscopedRuleBody` import at base-agent.ts:25. Optional, same helper, one more line: `parsed.body` for path-scoped rules at base-agent.ts:989 — rules are `.claude/rules/`, not CLAUDE.md, so this is consistency, not a doc requirement.

One line at 865-878: strip block comments before `trim()` and before the `MAX_NESTED_INSTRUCTION_FILE_BYTES` truncation, so a nested CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md delivered by a subdirectory read (base-agent.ts:1258-1262) obeys the same rule and comment bytes stop consuming the 10KB budget. Import the helper from '../agent/memory/memory-store.ts' (or hoist the helper to a leaf module if that import direction is unwanted — native-sources.ts already imports memory-store symbols such as MEMORY_IMPORT_DEPTH_LIMIT/parseMemoryImportPath/readMemoryFile).

Table-driven: block comment on its own line removed; multi-line comment removed; comment inside a ``` fence preserved; trailing inline `<!-- nessy:auto:2026-07-18 -->` preserved by this helper (and still removed later by stripAutoMemoryMarkers); and one readMemoryFile case where a 30-line comment header no longer pushes real entries past line 200.

One positive case: an instruction layer whose file contains a block comment produces a `<capability-layer>` body without it, and a fenced comment survives. One negative/boundary: a memory layer that is entirely comments yields no `<capability-layer>` and no eager InstructionsLoaded entry (assert whichever behaviour is chosen at base-agent.ts:1008 — decide it deliberately, it is hook-visible).

blastRadius: In-process only for the pinned block: `composePinnedCapabilityContext` is backend-agnostic and feeds every backend through `buildPinnedCapabilityContext` (base-agent.ts:883) — Pi (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts) and Claude (claude-agent.ts). The block is turn content, not persisted, so no wire/schema change there. THREE boundaries need care. (1) Persistence: MEMORY.md on disk is written by appendMemoryFile (memory-store.ts:120-131, mode 0600) and rewritten by memory-cleanup.ts, which prunes ONLY entries carrying the inline `<!-- nessy:auto:... -->` marker (memory-store.ts:159, producer packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/remember.ts:21-24). A whole-file (non-block-level) regex strip applied anywhere on the write path would silently destroy those markers and with them the dated cleanup — the helper must stay block-level and injection-only. (2) Capability inventory: readMemoryFile is also the import walker at native-sources.ts:427, so stripping changes which `@import` targets become inventory records — that alters capability keys visible in the snapshot the renderer receives (Sources list), even though contentHash/revision still hash raw bytes. (3) Hooks: emptying a layer changes the `InstructionsLoaded` payload set (base-agent.ts:1008-1013, tests packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/instructions-loaded.test.ts). Tests to re-run: agent/memory/__tests__/memory-store.test.ts, memory-cleanup.test.ts, agent/__tests__/base-agent.test.ts, rules-unscoped-launch.test.ts, instructions-loaded.test.ts, nested-instruction-traversal.test.ts, capabilities/__tests__/nested-instruction-discovery.test.ts, automations/automation-system.test.ts. Explicitly OUT of scope, do not route through the new helper: packages/shared/src/docs/source-guides.ts:79/98 and packages/session-tools-core/src/templates/loader.ts:61, which give leading comments meaning. Also unaffected: the Read tool, which must keep showing comments (memory.md:161) — it never goes through these seams. Imported-plugin path: plugin-bundled instruction/memory resources go through the same materializer.readText, so they get the same treatment for free.
userImpact: A user who follows Claude's documented practice and puts `<!-- maintainer note -->` in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md or MEMORY.md gets the opposite of what the doc promises: the note is sent to the model inside the pinned `<capability-layer>` block on every capability generation, it spends context tokens the doc says it will not, and the model can act on a line addressed to human maintainers (a stale 'TODO: drop this rule' comment reads as an instruction). Worse and silent: comment lines count against limits, so a MEMORY.md with a comment header loses real entries past line 200 on the fallback prompt path (prompts/system.ts:453-455, used when the pinned context is off), and a nested CLAUDE.md with comments gets truncated earlier at the 10KB nested budget. This repo's own AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md contain no HTML comments (grep -a), so it is latent here; it surfaces the moment a user or an imported Claude plugin ships an instruction file that uses them, and it surfaces immediately for anyone who moved a CLAUDE.md over from Claude Code, where the comments were free.
notes: Every cited file was read at the cited lines (base-agent.ts:855-1030 and 1235-1300, memory-store.ts:1-340, materializer.ts:155-200, native-sources.ts:395-470 and 760-880, prompts/system.ts:440-460, claude-agent.ts:287-308). Two adjacent gaps found while reading, deliberately NOT folded into the change list because they are separate divergences: (a) the 25KB half of memory.md:383's 'first 200 lines, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first' does not exist anywhere — grep for a byte cap returns nothing; (b) more consequentially, the LIVE pinned path applies no MEMORY.md load limit at all: memory layers reach the model through materializer.readText (base-agent.ts:977), which returns the whole file, and MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT has only two consumers (the legacy loadMemoryPromptBlock fallback and the native-sources import walker). So the 'strip before measurement' fix in readMemoryFile is correct but currently only affects the fallback prompt and import discovery. What I could not verify: the exact block-level boundary Claude implements (whether a leading-whitespace-indented `<!--` counts as block-level, and whether an indented 4-space code block also protects comments) — the page states the rule without a grammar, so the proposed definition is our reading of 'block-level'.
